Earned Leave (EL) builds up month‑by‑month according to where you are in your employment tenure:

| Employment stage | Accrual rate | When it becomes usable |
|------------------|--------------|------------------------|
| **Probation period** | **0.5 day per month** | The days you earn while on probation are **not** usable until you are confirmed in your role. |
| **After probation – before completing 1 year of service** | **0.5 day per month** (same as during probation) | The accrued balance can be used once you are confirmed. |
| **After you have completed 1 year of continuous service** (and have worked at least 240 days in that year) | **1.25 days per month** | These days are available for use immediately (subject to manager approval). |
| **Once you have the initial 15 days** (earned after the first year) | **1.25 days per month** continues | The monthly accrual keeps adding to your EL balance throughout your employment. |

**In short:**  

- While you’re on probation (and until you’re confirmed), you earn **0.5 day of Earned Leave each month**.  
- After you’ve completed one year of continuous service (with at least 240 working days in that year), the accrual jumps to **1.25 days per month**.  

These accrued days are added to your EL balance and can be taken (with the usual 7‑day advance application and manager approval) as long as you have enough balance.

Eligibility for a work‑from‑home (WFH) arrangement depends on your grade and employment status:

- **Permanent employees at grade L3 or higher** are covered by the policy and may work from home, provided they are not on probation and are not deployed at a client site (unless they receive a written waiver from the HR Director).  
- **Employees at grades L1 or L2**, employees who are still on probation, or employees who are working on‑site at a client location are **not automatically eligible** for WFH. They would need a specific written approval from the HR Director on a case‑by‑case basis.

So, if you are a permanent employee at **grade L3, L4, L5, L6, L7, L8, L9, or L10 (C‑Suite)** and you are not on probation or assigned to a client site, you are eligible for WFH under the policy. If your grade is **L1 or L2**, or you are on probation or at a client site, you would need special written approval to work from home.

**How to raise a POSH (Prevention of Sexual Harassment) complaint at Zyro Dynamics Pvt. Ltd.**

1. **Submit a written complaint**  
   • Send it to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) **by email or sealed letter**.  
   • It must be filed **within 3 months of the incident** (or of the last incident in a series).  
   • In exceptional cases you can ask the ICC, in writing, to extend this period by another 3 months, providing reasons.

2. **ICC acknowledges receipt**  
   • The ICC will confirm they have received your complaint **within 7 working days** and will forward a copy to the respondent.

3. **Respondent’s reply**  
   • The person accused (the respondent) is given **10 working days** to submit a written response to the ICC.

4. **Inquiry & hearings**  
   • The ICC then conducts an inquiry, hearing both parties, any witnesses, etc., in an environment that respects dignity. (No specific deadline is given for the completion of the inquiry, but the above steps are time‑bound.)

**Timeline at a glance**

| Step | Action | Deadline |
|------|--------|----------|
| 1 | Aggrieved person files written complaint (email or sealed letter) | **Within 3 months** of the incident (extendable by 3 months in exceptional cases) |
| 2 | ICC acknowledges receipt & forwards to respondent | **Within 7 working days** |
| 3 | Respondent submits written response | **Within 10 working days** |
| 4 | ICC conducts inquiry/hearings | No fixed deadline stated; proceeds after step 3 |

So, to raise a POSH complaint, write your complaint and send it to the ICC (email or sealed letter) within the 3‑month window, and the process will follow the above timeline.

- **1‑year cliff:** You won’t receive any vested options until you’ve completed one full year of service. At the end of that first year, a portion (typically 25 % of the total grant) vests all at once.  
- **Remaining 3 years:** After the cliff, the rest of the options vest gradually over the next three years (often on a monthly or quarterly basis, depending on the company’s specific implementation).

So, in short: **no vesting for the first year, then 25 % vests at the 1‑year mark, and the remaining 75 % vests evenly over the following three years.**
